title: Roll a mouse pad up and slip a paper band over it before it springs open
instruction: Roll the mouse pad up from one short edge and slide the paper band over the roll, so that the band holds it rolled. Then put the banded roll down, let go and move both arms away.
context: A loose rubber-backed pad springs open between turns. Start with the pad flat, wind it, and slide a stiff paperboard sleeve over the roll before releasing it. The result can be checked where the sleeve encloses the pad. Manufacturer packaging guidance documents rolled pads retained with bands (Darshion, Why Some Mouse Pads Warp After Shipping).
setup: Units mm. x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the robot's left, z up from the table top. Two YAM arms with parallel grippers (pads 94 apart when open), bases at (0, +305) and (0, -305), at their ready pose with grippers open; one overhead camera and one camera on each wrist. Wooden table top 1100 x 1300; nothing else is on it. 1) Carton: a closed corrugated cardboard box 280 long (x) x 220 wide (y) x 120 high, taped shut and fixed to the table, spanning x 270 to 550 and y +50 to +270. It is only a raised work surface: on it, a gripper can get under the pad's edge and at the end of the roll from the side. 2) Mouse pad: a plain cloth-topped rubber-foam mouse pad, 250 x 210 x 3, 105 g, blue cloth with a stitched border on top, black rubber underneath, flat (no curl from storage). It lies flat on the carton, cloth side up, long side along x: its near short edge at x 245, sticking out 25 over the carton's near edge; its right-hand long edge at y +40, sticking out 10 over the carton's right-hand edge; its top 123 above the table. Laid with 100 of its length over a table edge, the free end droops about 45; rolled up and let go, it springs open in about a second. 3) Paper band: a stiff ring of kraft paperboard, a 80 length cut square from a mailing tube: inside diameter 70, wall 3 (outside diameter 76), 39 g, open at both ends. The pad rolled from a short edge is 210 long and, rolled by the reference demonstration, 61 to 67 across while it is held, so the band goes over it with a few millimetres to spare; the rolled pad let go inside the band opens until it fills the bore. 4) Cradle: two V saddles 12 thick, at x 320 and x 360, each a V of two flat faces 45 long sloping 35 degrees from level, on a base strip fixed to the table (plywood or printed plastic). The band lies in the cradle with its axis along x, its middle at (340, -360), where a line is drawn on the base strip, its axis 50 above the table. The layout is the same in every trial. Pad stiffness, weights and friction are estimates to be checked against the bought pad and band (see README).
scoring: Scored on the state at the end of the trial (the run limit, or as soon as the 1.0 state is reached); nothing done earlier is held against the robot. On a real trial: note where the grippers are, then photograph the pad and band from above and end-on, and measure with a ruler. The pad counts as a roll if, seen end-on, it winds one way through at least one full turn, so that its two short edges overlap, and nowhere bends back the other way by more than 20 degrees: a pad folded flat in two or zigzag is not a roll, whatever is put round it. 0: the pad is not a roll, or less than a third of the band's length (27 mm) is over it. 0.3: the pad is a roll and the band is started on it: at least a third of the band's length (27 mm) is over the roll. 0.6: the pad is a roll and the band is on it: the whole roll passes through the band and stands at least 10 mm out of each of its ends. 1.0: in addition (a) the roll is square: measured along the roll, the turn that stands furthest out at one end and the turn that stands furthest back from it differ by no more than 10 mm; and (b) the banded roll has been put down and let go: both grippers' centre points have been at least 50 mm away from the band and from the pad for 2 seconds, so that nothing but the band is holding the roll shut. Where it is put down does not matter (the cradle, the table or the carton). A banded roll that is telescoped or still held scores 0.6. Possible scores: 0, 0.3, 0.6, 1.0. Inspect both exposed ends after release. Radial flaring beyond the sleeve is allowed; measure the 10 mm end offset along the roll axis, not across its diameter. The sleeve must surround all layers, and an open flap that unwinds the overlap fails the roll check.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Slip the band off the roll and lay the pad flat on the carton on its tape marks, cloth side up (near short edge 25 mm over the carton's near edge, right-hand long edge 10 mm over its right-hand edge). A pad that has kept a curl is rolled once the other way or left under a book until it lies flat with no edge more than 2 mm off the carton. Lay the band in the cradle with its middle on the line. Both arms to ready, grippers open. In simulation: seed 0, zero object jitter; pad and band are returned to their start state and the scorer starts fresh.
fidelity: Twenty-five hinged strips can roll, spring back and slide axially. Each strip is rigid across the width, so the model suppresses flaring beyond the sleeve. The paperboard sleeve is rigid. Its 70 mm bore is a specified test fixture, sized from the scripted roll. Springs and friction are estimates. No same-size hardware trial was performed.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0 in 2400 steps; scripted: 1.0 in 1429. One fixed-start run each.
